title: Entropy-consistent subsequence sampler and mini-batch orthogonalizer
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a new subsequence sampling primitive and an orthogonal mini-batcher to improve representative workload fidelity for mixed-length traffic; recommended opt-in for benchmark runs and nightly stability suites.
description: Motivation: existing workload generators underrepresent correlated subsequences leading to unstable tail estimates when short and long sequences coexist. This change introduces an entropy-consistent subsequence sampler that preserves observed local token-entropy structure while producing deterministic reproducible subsequences for replay. In parallel we introduce a mini-batch orthogonalizer that reorders and groups requests to maximize diversity within each batch without breaking sequence ordering guarantees for KV-cache warmup. Design: the sampler builds a lightweight statistical sketch per conversation window and draws subsequences using constrained resampling to maintain per-window entropy and marginal length distributions. The orthogonalizer forms micro-batches by solving a constrained assignment problem (approximate Hungarian with locality constraints) to ensure each mini-batch contains orthogonal token-paths, which improves GPU kernel utilization and reduces model internal contention. Backwards compatibility: default behavior for existing runners is unchanged; new primitives are exposed behind flags and a config section in the benchmark manifest. Test coverage: unit tests for sampler invariants, property tests to assert entropy-preservation statistics across synthetic corpora, integration tests for the orthogonalizer inside the multi-sequence runner, and end-to-end nightly regression jobs added. Impact: synthetic and replayed benchmarks show reduced p95 variance across runs and fewer extreme outliers. Usage: documented examples in bench-recipes/entropy-sampler.md and an arg to the runner: --subsequence-sampler=entropy-consistent, --orthogonalize-mini-batches=true. Related: aligns with ENG-4129 and supports follow-ups in BENCH-72 for mixed-length fidelity experiments.

review_comments: Miguel Rodriguez: This looks good overall but the orthogonalizer could increase request latency for some short-tail workloads. Can you add a config knob and measurement in the microbenchmarks to ensure we can toggle it with minimal friction?
Asha Patel: Added --orthogonalize-mini-batches flag and updated microbenchmarks to include latency and throughput sweeps. See perf commit that records p50/p95/p99 for both modes.
Priya Shah: Please add a short explanation in docs about how entropy is estimated and why it's stable for deterministic replays. The property tests are great but users will want intuition.
Asha Patel: Expanded docs/benchmarking/entropy-sampler.md with a short appendix on the sketch and parameters and a link to the property test harness to reproduce the stats.
Liam O'Connor: CI flaky test observed on arm builders (timing sensitive). Suggest making timeouts adaptive.
Asha Patel: Adjusted the integration test to use relative timeouts and retried with the ARM pool; CI now green.
performance_summary: Nightly mixed-length replay with sampler+orthogonalizer enabled reduced p95 variance across 10 runs by 32% and reduced extreme outliers (p99.9) by 48% on the heterogeneous GPU testbed. Average GPU SM utilization increased by 6% for micro-batched workloads. End-to-end mean latency impact was +3ms for very short single-token requests when orthogonalization is on, but throughput improved by 9% for typical 16-128 token sequences.
test_plan: Unit tests for sampler invariants, property tests over synthetic_corpora (statistical checks), integration test with multi_sequence_runner to assert KV cache correctness, microbenchmarks for latency/throughput sweep, nightly regression job added to CI pipeline to detect p95 drift and flaky variance. All tests run locally and in CI; results attached to CI run summary.
notes_for_backfill: When backfilling historical benchmark data, apply the entropy sketch with window size 256 and seed 42 to ensure deterministic subsequence selection. Backfill tooling script bench/scripts/backfill_entropy_consistent.py provided. Expect small shifts in historical p95 because subsequence sampling differs from previous uniform subsampler.
